newsitem.title: OMAN: Israel not attending Oman water conference.
newsitem.headline: Israel not attending Oman water conference.

text.p: Israel will not attend a forthcoming water conference in Oman due to apparent objections from Gulf Arab states, an official involved in organising the event said on Sunday.
"Israel will not take part in the the third Gulf Water Conference in Muscat," the official at the Omani Company for Exhibitions and International Trade told Reuters.
"Israel applied but the application was not discussed due to Gulf Arab participation in the conference," added the official who requested anonymity.
An Israeli official on Sunday confirmed that the Jewish state would not attend the three-day conference due to start on March 9.
"They informed us we cannot attend. We believe it is due to Saudi pressure. We are very sad about it," a spokesman for the Israel's Export Institute told Reuters in Jerusalem.
Israel has said it had received an invitation to the Oman conference.
Water -- a scarce resource in the Middle East -- is a bitter point of contention between Israelis and Palestinians as well as between other states in the region.
The Omani official said Israel had applied to participate in two other exhibitions scheduled to be held in Oman in April and November but expressed doubt it would attend.
"Israel's participation in the two forthcoming events is unlikely," he said without elaborating.
Oman in August opened a commercial interest office in Tel Aviv, making the energy-rich sultanate the first Gulf Arab state with economic representation in Israel.
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf Arab states in establishing economic ties with Israel after the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1993.
